guides.name: Washing machine is loud or shakes during spin
steps: Stop the cycle and spread the wet laundry evenly around the drum.
Untangle sheets or blankets; tangled bulky items throw the load off balance.
If the drum is packed tight, take some items out so clothes move freely.
Grip the top and rock the washer. All four feet should stay on the floor.
If a corner wobbles, loosen that leg's lock nut, if it has one, and turn the leg.
Once it stops rocking, tighten the lock nuts back against the washer.
New front-loader? Open the door and push the drum. If it feels solid, shipping bolts are still in.
Remove the bolts from the back with the supplied wrench, then plug the holes with the caps.
Run a small load to check that the shaking has stopped.
safety: Slide the washer gently; too much force can damage its feet.
Keep the shipping bolts in case you move the washer later.
stopIf: Squealing or grinding keeps happening even with a light load.
The noise or shaking continues after balancing and leveling.
You smell burning after the first two washes.

sources.quote: When clothes are distributed unevenly in the drum, it can cause the washer to become unstable during the spin cycle, leading to unwanted vibrations.

sources.quote: always try to load your washer with a balanced mix of items, placing heavier articles around lighter ones. Avoid tightly packing the load. Clothing should move freely within the washer.

sources.title: Washer is Vibrating, Walking or Moving - Product Help | Whirlpool
sources.quote: Grip the washer from the top and rock back and forth, ensuring all four feet are firmly on the floor. Repeat, rocking the washer from side to side.

sources.title: Washer is Vibrating, Walking or Moving - Product Help | Whirlpool
sources.quote: You can easily adjust the feet by twisting them until the washer is stable and doesn’t rock back and forth.

guides.name: Window air conditioner drips water into the room
aliases: air conditioner leaking into the room
window unit dripping on the floor
water coming out the front of my window ac
puddle under the window air conditioner
steps: First check where it drips; water dripping outside the window is normal.
Unplug the air conditioner before you look at it or work on it.
Wipe up any water around the unit so no one slips.
Check that the unit tilts slightly down toward the outside, about a quarter inch.
If the unit has drain holes underneath, clear them with a small brush.
Wash the air filter in warm water; add a little dish soap if very dirty.
Let the filter dry completely before you put it back.
If you see ice on the unit's coils, turn it off and let the ice melt.
Do not run it when it is below 70 degrees outside; the coils can ice up.
safety: Never drill holes in the bottom of the unit to let the water out.
Do not run the air conditioner without its filter in place.
Do not wash the filter in a dishwasher.
stopIf: The plugged-in unit is wet, or you are standing in water: do not touch it.
Still dripping inside after these checks? It is likely installed wrong; ask an installer.
Coils keep freezing? Low refrigerant can cause that; call a professional technician.

sources.title: Air Conditioner - Water Dripping Inside Room | GE Appliances
sources.quote: It is normal to see water dripping on the outdoor side of the Air Conditioner.

sources.title: I have noticed water dripping outside of my room air conditioner, is this normal? | Frigidaire
sources.quote: Water dripping outside is a normal function of the room air conditioner, especially during periods of excessive humidity.

sources.title: Troubleshooting a Leak in a TCL Window A/C Unit | TCL Support
sources.quote: Unplug the Unit: Always disconnect the air conditioner from the power source before inspecting or working on it.

sources.title: Troubleshooting a Leak in a TCL Window A/C Unit | TCL Support
sources.quote: Clean Up Water: If there's water around the unit, clean it up to avoid slipping or electrical hazards.

sources.title: Air Conditioner - Water Dripping Inside Room | GE Appliances
sources.quote: It should be level or tilted slightly to the outside (about 1/4 inch) so that any excess water will drip outside rather than leak into the room.

sources.title: Troubleshooting a Leak in a TCL Window A/C Unit | TCL Support
sources.quote: Tilt Angle: Ensure the air conditioner is installed with a slight tilt backward (towards the outside). This helps proper drainage of the condensed water.

sources.title: Troubleshooting a Leak in a TCL Window A/C Unit | TCL Support
sources.quote: Drain Holes: Ensure that the drain holes at the bottom of the unit are not blocked. Use a small brush or a piece of wire to clear any obstructions.

sources.title: Air Conditioner - Water Dripping Inside Room | GE Appliances
sources.quote: A dirty air filter can cause moisture to collect and drip on the floor inside the room.

sources.title: Air Conditioner - Cleaning the Filter | GE Appliances
sources.quote: You can wash the filter in warm water. If the filter is very dirty, add a little mild dish detergent in the warm water when you clean the filter.

sources.title: Air Conditioner - Cleaning the Filter | GE Appliances
sources.quote: You should not reinstall a damp filter. Wait for it to dry completely before installing it.

sources.title: Air Conditioner - Ice On Indoor Coils | GE Appliances
sources.quote: The quickest way to defrost the coils is turn the Air Conditioner off and allow the room air temperature to melt the ice.

sources.title: Troubleshooting a Leak in a TCL Window A/C Unit | TCL Support
sources.quote: If you notice ice build-up, turn off the unit and let it thaw completely before restarting.

sources.title: Air Conditioner - Ice On Indoor Coils | GE Appliances
sources.quote: The best way to prevent ice on coils is to not run the appliance if the outdoor temperature is below 70 degrees Fahrenheit.

sources.title: I have noticed water dripping outside of my room air conditioner, is this normal? | Frigidaire
sources.quote: Never drill holes into the bottom of the room air conditioner to remove water.

sources.title: Air Conditioner - Cleaning the Filter | GE Appliances
sources.quote: You should not use the Air Conditioner until the filter has been put back in place.

sources.title: Air Conditioner - Cleaning the Filter | GE Appliances
sources.quote: The filter cannot be cleaned in the Dishwasher.

sources.title: Fire Safety Information Sheet: Use Electrical Appliances Safely | Vermont Department of Public Safety
sources.quote: Do not touch an energized electrical appliance that is wet or if you are standing in water.

sources.title: I have noticed water dripping outside of my room air conditioner, is this normal? | Frigidaire
sources.quote: If water is dripping inside the room during the cooling, this is due to improper installation. Please refer to installation instructions or check with your local installer.

sources.title: Troubleshooting a Leak in a TCL Window A/C Unit | TCL Support
sources.quote: Low refrigerant levels can cause the evaporator coils to freeze. If you suspect a refrigerant issue, contact a professional technician for service.

sources.title: Troubleshooting a Leak in a TCL Window A/C Unit | TCL Support
sources.quote: A dirty air filter can restrict airflow, causing the evaporator coils to freeze and subsequently leak water when they thaw.

sources.title: Air Conditioner - Ice On Indoor Coils | GE Appliances
sources.quote: Ice on the indoor coils of an Air Conditioner can cause the appliance to stop cooling well. This may even cause the Air Conditioner to spit water or ice out of the front of the appliance.
